text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Transport Minister Rudolf Scholten wants to devise a new auction scheme for Austria's third mobile phone license.
- Far-right leader Joerg Haider celebrates 10th anniversary as head of the Freedom Party.
- Bank Girocredit to support Austria's ailing tourism industry by setting up a fund of one billion schillings.
- Heavy rainfalls cause floods in northern Austria.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima says there must be no changes to the Maastricht Treaty for European Monetary Union, rejects suggestions to include employment targets.
- Steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm is a long-term buy even though margins may fall in the second half, Investmentbank Austria says in a report.
- Austrian woods full of poisonous mushrooms after unusually wet summer.
- German bourse's record high last week could lure more investors back to the Vienna stock exchange, where analysts still see strong potential for gains.
- The mad cow crisis has hit Austria's farmers worse than Britain's, European Union farm commissioner Franz Fischler says.
- Franz Linser, far-right Freedom Party's top candidate for European Parliament elections on October 13, says he supports Austria joining NATO after a referendum.
